info.title: Trunk API
info.description: Payload contract for Trunk's Dynamic CI plan endpoints, projected from the Trunk API v2 OpenAPI document. Generated — do not edit by hand.

post.description:
Returns a per-job verdict for one workflow run: which jobs the change makes it safe to skip, and the evidence behind each decision. Normally called once per run by the [`trunk-io/dynamic-ci`](https://github.com/trunk-io/dynamic-ci) action, which maps the verdicts onto job outputs.

**Fail open.** A job absent from `jobs` must be run — that is the contract, not an error. Treat any non-200 the same way.

Send the changed files as `changedFiles` when you can compute them. Without it, Trunk fetches the diff between `baseSha` and `commitSha` through your GitHub App installation, which needs both commits on GitHub.

post.summary: Generate a CI skip plan for a Buildkite pipeline
post.description:
As [`dynamicCi.generatePlan`](#tag/dynamicCi/operation/dynamicCi.generatePlan), for a Buildkite pipeline. Identical request and response but for the workflow identity: Buildkite has no workflow file, so the pipeline is named by the organization and pipeline slugs its agent exports, and `jobKeys` are step `key:` values.

**Fail open.** A job absent from `jobs` must be run — that is the contract, not an error. Treat any non-200 the same way.

Send the changed files as `changedFiles` when you can compute them. Without it, Trunk fetches the diff between `baseSha` and `commitSha` through your GitHub App installation, which needs both commits on GitHub.

apiKey.description: An API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. An organization admin creates one in the Trunk app under **Settings → Developer → API Keys** and chooses the merge-queue permissions it holds; a key with none can read merge queues but change nothing. Those permissions scope merge queue only: every key can use the Flaky Tests and Dynamic CI endpoints, including their writes, whatever permissions it holds.

trunkToken.name: x-trunk-token
trunkToken.description:
A short-lived first-party token, sent in the `x-trunk-token` header. The `trunk` CLI sends one after `trunk auth login`, and the `trunk-io/login` action obtains one for a GitHub Actions run.

**A token from a GitHub Actions run can only upload impacted targets** (`PUT /v2/impacted-targets`), for the repository the run belongs to; every other endpoint refuses it.

baseSha.description: The commit to diff against. Null for a non-pull-request event, leaving diff-derived signals without evidence.

runId.description: `BUILDKITE_BUILD_ID`, recorded so the plan can later be scored against the build's outcome.

runAttempt.description: Which attempt this is, counting from 1. An agent's `BUILDKITE_RETRY_COUNT` counts from 0, so send it plus one.

prLabels.description: Ignored. Trunk reads the pull request's labels itself when the run asks for a plan. While the repository is in Learning mode, a pull request carrying a label on the repository's managed allow list (matched case-insensitively) is gated as if Dynamic CI were enabled. Accepted so that older clients still validate.

jobKeys.description: The step `key:` values to decide — what Trunk ingests from `buildkite.step.key`. **Empty means every keyed step in the pipeline** — the usual call.

ignoreSignals.description: Signals to drop from the tally. An unrecognized identifier is rejected, so a typo surfaces.

previousPath.description: The old path, for a `renamed` or `copied` file.

additions.description: Lines added. 0 for a binary file.

deletions.description: Lines removed. 0 for a binary file.

ChangedFileStatus.description: How the file changed. The values GitHub reports, so its `status` can be passed through. `changed` (a type change, such as a file becoming a symlink) is read as `modified`.

base.description: The commit or ref the diff was taken from.

totalFiles.description: How many files changed, before the 200-file cap.

totalAdditions.description: Lines added across every changed file, before the cap.

totalDeletions.description: Lines removed across every changed file, before the cap.

files.description: The first 200 changed files. Must hold exactly `min(totalFiles, 200)` entries.

ChangedFiles.description: The files changed between `base` and `commitSha`, diffed from their merge base (`base...commitSha`). No file contents. **Omit it if you cannot compute the diff; never send an empty list in its place.** An empty list says nothing changed, which is the strongest evidence to skip. When it is absent, Trunk fetches the diff through your GitHub App installation.

jobs.description: One verdict per job. **A job absent from this list must be run** — the documented fail-safe, and how an unrecognized job, a merge-queue branch, and a not-yet-enabled organization are all reported.

baseSha.description: The commit to diff against. Null for a non-pull-request event, leaving diff-derived signals without evidence.

runId.description: `github.run_id`, recorded so the plan can later be scored against the run's outcome.

prLabels.description: Ignored. Trunk reads the pull request's labels itself when the run asks for a plan. While the repository is in Learning mode, a pull request carrying a label on the repository's managed allow list (matched case-insensitively) is gated as if Dynamic CI were enabled. Accepted so that older clients still validate.

jobKeys.description: The `jobs:` keys to decide. **Empty means every keyed job in the workflow** — the usual call.

ignoreSignals.description: Signals to drop from the tally. An unrecognized identifier is rejected, so a typo surfaces.

workflowPath.description: From `github.workflow_ref`; identifies the workflow whose jobs are in scope.

jobKey.description: The workflow's declarative `jobs:` key — what `github.job` reports and what an `if:` names.

summary.description: One-line rationale for the verdict, safe to show to a user.
summary.example: Skipping: no changed file has ever broken this job.

signals.description: The audit trail behind `summary`, abstentions included.

code.description: A stable identifier for the condition, safe to branch on. Today: `ORG_NOT_ENABLED`, `REPO_NOT_ENABLED`, `REPO_IN_SHADOW_MODE`, `ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE`, `WORKFLOW_NOT_RECOGNIZED`. `MERGE_QUEUE_BRANCH` is retired and no longer sent — merge-queue runs now carry real per-job verdicts. **An open set** — fall back to `message` for a code you do not recognize.

message.description: The condition in prose, safe to show to a user verbatim.
message.example: Every job will run: Dynamic CI is not enabled for this organization. Contact Trunk to turn it on.

PlanNotice.description: Why this plan has the shape it does. **Absent unless every job runs for a reason `jobs` cannot express**: a not-yet-enabled organization or repository, a merge-queue branch, an engine outage, or a workflow Trunk has not enumerated — all indistinguishable otherwise, and all arriving as an empty `jobs` when you request a whole workflow. `REPO_IN_SHADOW_MODE` is the exception: the plan is fully populated and each `summary` is the recommendation the job would have received, but nothing is allowed to skip.

host.description: Disambiguates GitHub.com from a GitHub Enterprise Server host. `github.com` is the only supported value today.

SignalRecommendation.description: One signal's contribution. `MUST_RUN` and `NEVER_RUN` are hard verdicts (a single one decides, with `MUST_RUN` winning a tie); `VOTE_RUN` and `VOTE_NO_RUN` are weighted votes. `INCOMPLETE` means the signal applies but lacks evidence — two of them fail the job safe to running. `ABSTAIN` means the signal does not apply at all and is excluded from the tally entirely, which is what makes it different from `INCOMPLETE`.

message.description: Human-readable evidence for this signal's contribution.
message.example: Reliably green (98.0% pass rate over 240 runs).

ignored.description: True when `ignoreSignals` excluded this signal from the tally. Its `recommendation` is what it would have contributed.

SignalType.description: Which independent signal produced a contribution to a job's verdict. These identifiers are also what `ignoreSignals` accepts.
